Disclosure  to  Promote  the  Right  To  Information 

Whereas  the  Parliament  of  India  has  set  out  to  provide  a  practical  regime  of  right  to 
information  for  citizens  to  secure  access  to  information  under  the  control  of  public  authorities, 
in  order  to  promote  transparency  and  accountability  in  the  working  of  every  public  authority, 
and  whereas  the  attached  publication  of  the  Bureau  of  Indian  Standards  is  of  particular  interest 
to  the  public,  particularly  disadvantaged  communities  and  those  engaged  in  the  pursuit  of 
education  and  knowledge,  the  attached  public  safety  standard  is  made  available  to  promote  the 
timely  dissemination  of  this  information  in  an  accurate  manner  to  the  public.

FOREWORD 

This  Indian  Standard  (  First  Revision)  was  adopted  by  the  Bureau  of  Indian  Standards,  after  the  draft  finah/cdbv  ihe 
Steel  Tubes,  Pipes  and  Fittings  Sectional  Committee  had  been  approved  b\  the  Metallurgical  Engineering  Division 
Council 

This  standard  was  First  published  in  1969  to  meet  the  increased  application  of  spiral  welded  pipes  The  revision  ol  Uns 
standard  has  been  prepared  incorporating  the  following  main  modifications 

a)  To  bring  it  in  line  with  latest  practice  of  spiral  welded  pipes  lor  general  use 

b)  Ladle  and  product  analysis  for  the  material  has  been  specified 

c)  Tensile  test  requirements  have  been  modified 

d)  Hydrostatic  test  requirements  have  been  modified 

c)     The  standard  has  been  brought  in  line  with  other  International  Standards  on  welded  steel  pipes 

In  preparation  of  this  standard  assistance  has  been  taken  (roni  the  following  publications 

ASTM-A-114         Specification  for  electric  fusion  (Arc)  welded  steel  plate  pipe  si/c  400  mm  and  o\  cr 

ASTM-A-252  Specification  for  welded  and  seamless  steel  pipe  piles 

FoTthc  purpose  of  deciding  whether  a  particular  requirement  of  this  standard  is  complied  with  the  final  value  observed 
or  calculated,  expressing  the  result  of  a  test  or  analvsis.  shall  be  rounded  oil  in  accordance  with  IS  2  I960  Rules  for 
rounding  of  numerical  values  (revised)  The  number  of  significant  places  retained  in  the  rounded  off  value  should  be 
the  same  as  thai  of  the  specified  value  in  this  standard

t  his  standard  covers  the  requirements  of  spiral  seam 
Added  steel  pipe  over  457  mm  dia  and  upto  2  000 
aim  dia  with  wall  thickness  upto  12  5  mm  inclusive

of  pipe  for  various  purposes  is  dependent  on  its 
dimensions,  properties  and  condition  of  serv  ice  The 
purr>  for  which  the  pipe  is  intended  should  be  stated 
in  t\      nquiry  and  order

SUPPLY  OF  MATERIAL 

General  requirements  relating  to  the  supply  of  spiral 
welded  pipes  shall  conform  to  IS  1387 

4  MANUFACTURE 

4.1  Pipe  shall  be  made  from  steel  produced  b>  the 
open  hearth  or  electric  or  one  of  the  basic  o\>gen 
processes  Other  processes  may  be  used  by  agreement 
with  the  purchaser 

4.2  The  pipes  shall  be  made  by  rolling  a  strip,  sheet 
:>r  plate  so  that  a  helical  seam  is  formed  around  the 

circumference  of  the  pipe  The  helical  seam  shall  be 
velded  by  one  of  the  following  processes 

a)     Electric  fusion  butt  welding  internally  and 
...w  aic  welding  externally 

b;     electric  resistance  welding 

c)     Automatic  submerged  -arc  welding  using  at 
least  two  weld  passes,  one  of  which  shall  be 


on  the  inside  of  the  pipe  All  end  welding 
of  spiral  seams  of  submerged-arc  welding 
pipe  if  not  done  b>  automatic  submerged- 
arc  welding,  shall  be  done  b\  a  procedure 
and  welder  qualified  in  accordance  with 
Annex  A 

4.3  The  coil  or  sheet  used  for  manufacture  oi  the 
pipe  shall  be  trimmed  to  the  proper  width  jnd  gncn 
special  edge  treatment  required  bv  the  welding  process 
The  material  then  shall  be  rolled  so  that  a  helical  seam 
is  formed  around  the  circumference  of  the  pipe  The 
electric  arc  welding  operation  performed  lo  fuse  or 
seal  the  edges  or  surface  of  helical  seam  shall  produce 
generally  uniform  weld

6.2     Flattening  Tests 

6.2. 1  For  electric  resistance-welded  pipes  produced 
in  single  lengths,  the  crop  ends  cut  from  each  end  of 


each  length  shall  be  flattened  between  parallel  plates 
until  opposiie  walls  of  the  pipe  meet  The  tests  irom 
each  end  shall  be  made  alternately  with  the  welds  at 
0°and  90  (point  of  ma  Milium  bending)  No  opening 
in  the  weld  shall  take  place  until  the  distance  between 
the  plates  is  less  than  two-thirds  of  the  original  outside 
diameter  of  the  pipe,  and  no  cracks  or  breaks  in  the 
metal,  elsewhere  than  in  the  weld,  shall  occur  until 
the  distance  between  the  plates  is  less  than  one-thud 
of  the  original  outside  diameter  of  the  pipe  Also 
evidence  of  laminations  or  burnt  metal  shall  not 
dev  clop  during  the  entire  flattening  operation  If  am 
crop  end  fails  to  conform  to  these  requirements 
additional  lests  shall  be  made  on  specimens  cut  Irom 
the  same  end  oi  the  same  length  of  pipe  until  the 
requirements  are  met  except  that  the  finished  pipe 
shall  not  be  shorter  than  XO  percent  of  its  length  after 
the  initial  cropping  Precautions  shall  be  taken  so 
that  the  crop  ends  can  be  identified  with  respcel  to 
the  length  of  pipe  from  which  thev  were  cut 

6.2.2  For  elcclric-resistancc-wclded  pipe  produced 
in  multiple  lengths  and  subsequently  cut  into  single 
lengths,  the  crop  ends  cut  from  each  end  of  each 
multiple  length  shall  be  flattened  between  parallel 
plates  until  opposite  walls  of  the  pipe  meet  The  tests 
shall  be  made  with  the  weld  at  90°  (point  of  maximum 
bending)  The  tests  shall  also  be  made  on  two 
intermediate  rings  cut  from  each  multiple  length  of 
pipe  with  the  weld  at  0"  If  anv  of  the  specimens  fail 
to  conform  to  the  requirments  specified  in  6.2. 1  the 
manufacturer  mav  elect  to  make  rctcstscut  from  each 
end  of  each  individual  length  as  provided  in  6.2.1 
Rctests  shall  be  made  with  the  welds  alternateh  at 
0°  and  90°

7  HYDROSTATIC  TEST 

Unless  otherwise  specified  each  length  of  the  pipe 
shall  be  tested  at  mill  to  a  hydrostatic  pressure,  equal 
to  a  minimum  of  150  percent  of  working  pressure 
required  In  no  case  the  maximum  stress  produced 
exceeds  40  percent  of  minimum  ultimate  tensile 
strength  envisaged  in  the  steel 

NOTh  Steel   tensile   strength   may   be  assumed   as 

410  MI'a  normally  and  unless  otherwise  agreed 

The  pressure  shall  be  calculated  from  the  following 
equation 


P   =     2  \t/D 


where 


P     -    test  pressure  MPa, 

v     =    stress  in  MPa  (normally  40  percent  of 
410  MPa  that  is,  164  MPa), 

/     =    specified  wall  thickness  in  mm,  and 

D     -    specified  outside  diameter  in  mm 

8  PERMISSIBLE  VARIATIONS   IN 
DIMENSIONS 

8.1  Lengths 

Steel  pipe  shall  be  supplied  in  single  random  length 
between  4  to  7  m  or  double  random  length  of  7  to 
1 4  m  For  order  over  200  metres  it  shall  be  permissible 
to  supply  short  random  length  of  2  to  4  m  provided 
total  or  such  lengths  does  not  exceed  7  5  percent  of 
supply 

8.2  Thickness  and  Diameter 

8.2.1  The  tolerance  on  wall  thickness  shall  be  +15 

percent  and  -12  5  percent  unless  otherwise  agreed 
in  plate/coil  specification 

8.2.2  The  tolerance  on  outside  diameter  of  pipe  shall 
be  as  follows 

Upto  1  000  mm   OD  =  ±0  75  percent 

Over  1  000  mm    OD  =  ±  1  percent 

8.2.3  The  ovahtyofpipe  shall  be  within  ±0  75  percent 

9  FINISH 

The  finished  pipe  shall  be  reasonably  straight  free 
from  injurious  defects  and  with  ends  prepared  as 
specified  in  the  purchase  order 


9.1  The  pipe  shall  be  substantially  round,  outside 
circumference  of  the  pipe  shall  not  van  more  than 

I  0  percent  from  the  nominal  outside  circumference 
based  on  diameter  specified 

10   REPAIR  BY  WELDING 

Injurious  defects  in  pipe  wall  provided  their  depth 
does  not  exceed  one  third  of  the  specified  wall 
thickness  shall  be  repaired  bv  welding  Defects  in 
the  welds,  such  as  sweats  and  leaks,  unless  othcrw  isc 
specified  shall  be  repaired  or  piece  rejected  at  the 
option  of  the  manufacturer  Repairs  of  this  nature 
shall  be  made  by  completely  removing  the  defect 
cleaning  the  cavity  and  then  welding 

All  repaired  pipe  shall  be  re-tested  hydraulicallv  in 
accordance  with  7 

II  PROTECTIVE  COATING 

After  pipe  is  subjected  to  hydrostatic  test  if  so 
specified  b>  the  purchaser  outside  surface  ma\  be 
given  a  protective  coating  of  the  kind  specified  b\ 
the  purchaser 

12  MARKING 

Each  length  of  pipe  shall  be  legibly  marked  with 
appropriate  symbol  stenciling  or  painting  to  show  the 
name  or  brand  of  manufacturer,  size  (wall  thickness 
and  diameter) 

12.1  The  pipes  may  also  be  marked  with  BIS 
Certification  Mark 

12.1.1  The  use  of  the  Standard  Mark  is  governed  b\ 
the  provisions  of  Bureau  oj  Indian  Standatd  let 
1 986,  and  the  Rules  and  Regulations  made  thereunder 
The  details  of  conditions  under  which  the  licence  lor 
the  use  of  Standard  Mark  may  be  granted  to 
manufacturers  or  producers  may  be  obtained  from 
the  Bureau  of  Indian  Standards 

13  INFORMATION    TO    BE   SUPPLIED    BY 
THE  PURCHASER 

The  purchaser  shall  state  in  his  enquiry  or  order 

a)  Outside  diameter,  nominal  thickness  and  total 
length  of  pipe  required, 

b)  Purpose  for  which  pipes  are  intended  to  be 
used 

c)  Length  range  in  individual  tube  to  be  supplied 

d)  Working  pressure  for  the  pipe  envisaged  in 
com  eying  fluid,  if  anv. 

e)  Whether  any  protective  coating  is  needed 
on  outside  surface. 

f)  Whether  he  himself  or  representative  w  ishes 
to  witness  hydrostatic  test  of  individual  pipe 
and 

g)  Anv  special  markings  required

ANNEX   A 

(  Clause  4  2  ) 
REPAIR-WELDING  PROCEDURE  AND  WELDER  PERFORMANCE  TESTS 


A-l    GENERAL 

A-l.l  All  manual  and  semi-automatic  submerged- 
arc  and  gas-shielded-arc  repair  welds  and  manual  and 
semi-automatic  metallic-arc  repair  welds  using  coated 
electrodes  shall  be  made  according  lo  a  tested 
procedure  and  bv  a  repair-welder  tested  in  a  flat 
position  as  specified  in  A-2  and  A-3  When  the  base 
metal  temperature  of  the  material  to  be  repair  welded 
is  below  ]0°C,  submerged-arc,  gas-shielded-arc  or 
manual  metallic-arc  methods  with  low  hydrogen 
electrodes  shall  be  used  for  the  repair-welding  test 
The  manufacturer  shall  maintain  a  record  of  the 
procedure  and  performance  test  results  Test  welds 
mav  be  made  either  on  plate  stock  or  pipe  stock  at 
the  option  of  the  manufacturer 

A-2  REPAIR-WELDING  PROCEDURE  TESTS 

A-2. 1  Repair-welding  procedure  tests  ore  required 
on  two  specimens  from  each  test  of  even  grade  and 
on  material  which  is  on  the  high  side  of  the  chemical 
specification  and  which  is  at  least  as  thick  as  the  pipe 
on  which  welds  arc  to  be  made  The  repair-welding 
procedure  test  shall  be  made  at  a  temperature  at  or 
below  the  lowest  temperature  at  which  repair  welds 
arc  made 

A-2. 2  Transverse  Tensile  Test 

The  transverse  tensile  test  specimen  (  see  Fig  4  ) 
shall  be  approximately  18  mm  wide  and  shall  have 
the  transverse  metallic-arc  butt  weld  perpendicular 
to  the  longitudinal  axis  at  the  centre  of  the  test 
specimen  The  weld  reinforcement  shall  be  removed 
from  both  faces  The  ultimate  tensile  strength  shall 
be  at  least  equal  to  the  minimum  specified  for  the 
grade 

A-2.3    Longitudinal  Tensile  —  Elongation  Test 

The  longitudinal  tensile-elongation  test  specimen  shall 
conform  to  Fig  5  The  weld  shall  be  made  in  a  groove 
as  shown  The  elongation  after  complete  rupture  of 
the  test  specimen  in  tension  shall  be  at  least  equal 
to  the  minimum  elongation  specified  for  the  grade 

A-2.4    Transverse  Guided  —  Bend  Test 

The  transverse  guided-bend  test  specimen  shall 


conform  to  Fig  (>  The  weld  shall  be  made  in  a  groove 
is  shown  The  specimen  shall  be  placed  on  the  die 
with  the  weld  at  mid-span  and  shall  be  bent 
approximateh  180°  in  a  jig  in  accordance  with 
Pig  t>  with  the  exposed  surface  of  the  weld  in  tension 
The  bend  test  shall  be  considered  acceptable  il 

a)  No  crack  or  other  defect  exceeding  ^  mm 
in  am  direction  is  present  in  the  weld  met  il 
or  between  the  weld  and  the  pipe  meial  iltci 
bending  Cracks  which  originate  along  11k 
edges  of  the  specimen  during  tcsium  mcl 
which  tire  less  than  6  ^  mm  measured  m  m\ 
direction  shall  not  be  considered 

b)  The  specimen  cracks  or  Iraclurcs  durum 
bending  and  the  exposed  surface  shows 
complete  penetration  and  fusion  throughout 
the  entire  thickness  of  the  weld  specimen 
not  more  than  1  gas  pocket  per  square  em 
with  the  greatest  dimension  not  exceeding 
1  6  mm  and  no  slag  inclusions  greater  than 
()  8  nun  deep  or  ~\  mm  wide  and  separated 
bv  at  least  H  mm  of  sound  metal  (if 
necessarv  the  specimen  shall  be  broken  ,ip  wt 
lo  permit  examination  ol  the  fracture  ) 

A-2.5    Nick-Break  Test 

The  nick-break  specimen  shall  conform  lo  Fig  7  The 
weld  shall  be  made  in  a  groove  as  shown  The  specimen 
shall  be  hacksaw -notched  from  both  edges  ai  ihc  centre 
of  the  weld  and  shall  be  broken  bv  pulling  or  hammer 
blows  at  the  centre  or  one  end  The  exposed  surface 
of  the  specimen  shall  be  considered  acceptable  il  it 
shows  not  more  than 

a)  One  gas  pocket  for  nominal  wall  thicknesses 
of  6  is  mm  and  less 

b)  Two  gas  pockets  for  nominal  wall  thicknesses 
of  12  7  mm  or  less  but  greater  than  <>  ^ 
nun 

c)  Three  gas  pockets  for  nominal  wall 
thicknesses  greater  than  12  7  mm  The 
greatest  dimension  of  a  gas  pocket  shall  not 
exced  1  6  mm  Slag  inclusion  shall  be 
separated  bv  at  least  13  mm  of  sound  met  il 
and  shall  be  not  greater  than  0  8  mm  deep 
or  1  mm  wide

rclcsts  shall  be  required  if  made  immediately,  or  (wo

instructions  in  the  practice  before  making  a  retcst 
All  rctcsts  shall  conform  to  the  requirements  specified 
Further  performance  tests  arc  required  at  a  minimum 


of  onc-\car  nuer\als  and  also  if  the  repair-ucldcr 
is  not  engaged  in  the  tested  rcpair-uclding  procedure 
for  a  period  of  three  months  or  more  or  if  there  is 
some  specific  reason  to  question  his  abilit\  Both  oi 
the  following  tests  shall  be  made 

a)  Transverse  guidcd-bend  test  as  stipulated 
under  welding  procedure  test  (  \ee  A-2.4  ) 
and

procedure  test  (  see  A-2.5  )

Bureau  of  Indian  Standards 

BIS  is  a  statutory  institution  established  under  the  Bureau  of  Indian  Standards  Act,  1 986  to  promote  harmonious 
development  of  the  activities  of  standardization,  marking  and  quality  certification  of  goods  and  attending  to 
connected  matters  in  the  country. 

Copyright 

BIS  has  the  copyright  of  all  its  publications.  No  part  of  these  publications  maybe  reproduced  in  any  form  without 
the  prior  permission  in  writing  of  BIS.  This  does  not  preclude  the  free  use,  in  the  course  of  implementing  the 
standard,  of  necessary  details,  such  as  symbols  and  sizes,  type  or  grade  designations.  Enquiries  relating  to 
copyright  be  addressed  to  the  Director  (Publications),  BIS. 

Review  of  Indian  Standards 

Amendments  are  issued  to  standards  as  the  need  arises  on  the  basis  of  comments.  Standards  are  also  reviewed 
periodically;  a  standard  along  with  amendments  is  reaffirmed  when  such  review  indicates  that  no  changes  are 
needed;  if  the  review  indicates  that  changes  are  needed,  it  is  taken  up  for  revision.  Users  of  Indian  Standards 
should  ascertain  that  they  are  in  possession  of  the  latest  amendments  or  edition  by  referring  to  the  latest  issue 
of  'BIS  Handbook1  and  'Standards  :  Monthly  Additions'. 

This  Indian  Standard  has  been  developed  from  Doc    No  MTD  19(1271  )
